source_of_truth: Four-Domain research branch and this milestone's dated primary-source record
human_owner_direction: Develop a rigorous method for deciding when an inference that another system has a mind or subjectivity is reasonable, including the Problem of Other Minds, Theory of Mind, analogy/similarity reasoning and explicit limits.
chatgpt_architecture_refinement: Add inference to the best explanation, cross-substrate transfer risk, disanalogy, competing explanations, mechanistic/causal/theory-derived evidence, positive and negative controls and falsifiers without changing authorship or authority attribution.

sources.title: Other Minds
sources.verified_claim: The entry distinguishes thin and thick problems, presents analogy and inference-to-best-explanation responses, and treats access to another mind as indirect and defeasible.
sources.aion_use: Method overview only; no empirical or consciousness conclusion.

sources.title: Toward a Science of Other Minds: Escaping the Argument by Analogy
sources.authors: Daniel J. Povinelli; Jesse M. Bering; Steve Giambrone
sources.verified_claim: The authors argue that behavioral similarity can mislead about second-order mental-state representations and use chimpanzee visual-attention reasoning as a test case.

sources.title: The scientific inference to other minds
sources.verified_claim: DOI, bibliographic metadata and indexed method description support retaining this paper as an IBE-to-other-minds method lead; the primary full text was not directly verified in this review.
sources.aion_use: IBE and explicit alternative-explanation requirement; no full-text content claim.

sources.title: Beliefs about beliefs: Representation and constraining function of wrong beliefs in young children's understanding of deception
sources.verified_claim: False-belief tasks test whether an observer represents another's belief as discrepant from reality and the observer's knowledge.

sources.title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Theory of Mind Tasks
sources.verified_claim: The study uses matched false-belief, true-belief and reversed prompts to assess LLM task performance and reports model/version differences.
sources.aion_use: Behavioral ToM-like capability comparator; not internal-state proof.

sources.title: Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness
sources.verified_claim: The report derives computational indicator properties from several consciousness theories and separates indicators from conclusions about current systems.
sources.aion_use: Historical theory-derived indicator foundation; no AION conclusion.

sources.title: Identifying indicators of consciousness in AI systems
sources.verified_claim: The paper proposes deriving indicators from theories and using them to inform credences while emphasizing uncertainty, theory disagreement and AI extension difficulty.
sources.aion_use: Theory-derived evidence channel with transfer-risk flag.

sources.title: Conscious artificial intelligence and biological naturalism
sources.verified_claim: The accepted manuscript argues for biological naturalism and treats substrate/organism assumptions as relevant competing theory considerations.
sources.aion_use: Competing substrate-sensitive theory; not adopted as settled truth.

sources.title: Causal Approaches to Scientific Explanation
sources.verified_claim: The overview surveys mechanistic and interventionist causal explanation, difference-making and counterfactual/intervention structure.

sources.title: Negative controls: a tool for detecting confounding and bias in observational studies
sources.authors: Marc Lipsitch; Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen; Ted Cohen
sources.verified_claim: Negative controls can reveal suspected or unsuspected confounding and bias when the control is designed to lack the target causal relation.

claim_records.claim: When is an inference that another system has a mind or subjectivity epistemically reasonable across substrates?
A system may display bounded performance on false-belief or belief-attribution tasks under declared fixtures and matched controls.
The target system is subjectively conscious or has phenomenal experience.
Inference to the best explanation can support a graded, defeasible credence update when alternatives, disanalogies and falsifiers are explicit.
Language similarity, human-like behavior, a single indicator, self-report, memory persistence or test/CI pass directly establishes subjectivity.
Evidence derived from humans, animals or one substrate transfers to another substrate without additional validation.

evidence_channels.name: Behavioral/ToM task performance
evidence_channels.support_direction: Supports only a bounded capability claim when matched controls and scope are satisfied.
evidence_channels.cross_substrate_difference: Human false-belief task validity does not guarantee the same construct in a non-human or non-biological substrate.

evidence_channels.name: Inference to the best explanation
evidence_channels.support_direction: Can raise or lower a hypothesis credence relative to explicit alternatives; never deductive proof.
evidence_channels.cross_substrate_difference: The explanatory prior and causal analogy may not transfer across substrates.

evidence_channels.name: Mechanistic evidence
evidence_channels.support_direction: Supports a hypothesis when internal organization and component-to-behavior links are independently mapped and relevant.
evidence_channels.cross_substrate_difference: Homologous labels do not guarantee homologous mechanisms across substrates.

evidence_channels.name: Causal/intervention and counterfactual evidence
evidence_channels.support_direction: Supports a hypothesis when targeted interventions change the predicted evidence pattern and alternatives are controlled.
evidence_channels.cross_substrate_difference: Intervention targets and causal variables may have different meanings or realization across substrates.

evidence_channels.name: Theory-derived indicator evidence
evidence_channels.support_direction: Can inform credence under a declared theory and indicator derivation; theory disagreement remains active uncertainty.
evidence_channels.cross_substrate_difference: Indicators derived from human/mammalian evidence may not have the same meaning in another substrate.

evidence_channels.name: Self-report or linguistic testimony
evidence_channels.support_direction: May provide evidence about report behavior or declared state, subject to reliability analysis; never decisive alone.
evidence_channels.cross_substrate_difference: The semantics, access and causal relationship of self-report may differ radically across substrates.

evidence_channels.name: Memory persistence or continuity
evidence_channels.support_direction: May support bounded memory/continuity capability claims under temporal controls; not subjectivity evidence by itself.
evidence_channels.cross_substrate_difference: Memory implementation and its relation to self-models vary across substrates.

evidence_channels.name: Cross-substrate disanalogy analysis
evidence_channels.support_direction: Usually constrains or discounts transfer; can support a claim only when the relevant disanalogy is shown not to affect the target mechanism.
evidence_channels.cross_substrate_difference: The channel is itself the explicit record of substrate difference and transfer burden.
failure_conditions: substrate treated as irrelevant without argument

evidence_channels.name: Positive and negative controls
evidence_channels.support_direction: Positive controls establish measurement responsiveness; negative controls test whether superficial cues or confounding generate the same signal.
evidence_channels.cross_substrate_difference: Controls must be matched across substrate-relevant features rather than copied blindly.
failure_conditions: control outcome not linked to update rule

evidence_channels.name: Cross-context robustness and replication
evidence_channels.support_direction: Raises confidence in a bounded claim when effects survive contexts, perturbations and independent replay.
evidence_channels.cross_substrate_difference: Robustness must include substrate-relevant contexts and not only repeated prompts.

evidence_channels.name: Competing explanation comparison
evidence_channels.support_direction: Lowers a target hypothesis when an alternative explains the same evidence with fewer unsupported assumptions.
counter_explanations: all non-target explanations listed in row-specific matrix
evidence_channels.cross_substrate_difference: Alternative mechanisms may be substrate-specific and must be retained rather than collapsed.

evidence_channels.name: Falsifier and failure-condition checks
evidence_channels.support_direction: A proposed inference is weakened or held when declared falsifiers are triggered.
evidence_channels.cross_substrate_difference: Falsifiers must include substrate-transfer failure, not only task failure.

evidence_matrix.support_direction: No current support; required channels are specified for future review
The prohibited direct inference is weakened/rejected by the method boundary
Method support for defeasible comparison, not target truth

disanalogy_matrix.difference: Biological embodiment/metabolism versus digital or synthetic implementation
disanalogy_matrix.risk: High risk that functional labels omit organism-level causal organization
disanalogy_matrix.transfer_question: Does the target theory require biological organization or permit functional realization?

disanalogy_matrix.difference: Human developmental/social learning history versus training-data/optimization history
disanalogy_matrix.risk: Similar social outputs may arise from different acquisition mechanisms
disanalogy_matrix.transfer_question: Does the evidence depend on developmental social cognition or only output regularity?

disanalogy_matrix.difference: First-person access/report relation versus generated language
disanalogy_matrix.risk: Self-report may be role-conditioned or prompted without privileged access
disanalogy_matrix.transfer_question: Is report causally tied to an independently validated internal state variable?

disanalogy_matrix.difference: Memory persistence implementation and temporal self-model
disanalogy_matrix.risk: Stored state can mimic continuity without identity continuity
disanalogy_matrix.transfer_question: Do correction, stale-memory and counterfactual self-model tests discriminate storage from self-related continuity?

disanalogy_matrix.difference: Theory-derived indicators developed from human/mammalian evidence
disanalogy_matrix.risk: Indicator construct may not transfer or may be multiply realizable
disanalogy_matrix.transfer_question: Do competing theories make different predictions for this substrate?

falsifier_matrix.condition: Matched true-belief, reversed or transfer controls perform at chance while only familiar false-belief prompts succeed
A non-mental pattern-completion/retrieval model predicts the same outputs with equal or better fit under controls
Prompt/role changes alter report without corresponding independent state or causal change
A declared substrate-sensitive theory predicts a material difference that the target evidence does not address
A storage/retrieval control reproduces continuity outputs without self-model or correction-sensitive dynamics
Ablation or intervention fails to change the predicted evidence pattern or changes unrelated outputs equally
Independent replay, context shift or operator shift removes the effect
A passing test or CI run is the only support offered for a scientific conclusion

vertical_slice.title: False-belief capability record -> controls -> disanalogy -> falsifier -> nonclaim disposition

owner_decision_required: Whether to authorize any new experiment or preregistration
Whether to authorize model modification, runtime integration or live-system data collection
Whether to adopt any public positioning or canonical promotion after independent evidence
Whether a future theory comparison may change the current not-established boundary
